hidden_items.checklist_item: H3 - Overload or dynamic dispatch not locally evident (the indexed read)
hidden_items.why: Local site: `return items.get(0).tag();`, at the `items.get(0)` sub-expression. CORRECTION (cross-language consistency audit): the previous record charged H3 only for `tag()`'s dispatch and missed the indexed read. `get` is invoked on an interface-typed receiver, so JLS 26 15.12.4.4 selects the body from the RUN-TIME class of the object `List.of(new A(), new B())` returned - a java.util.ImmutableCollections.ListN, which the local site does not name and the Java SE 26 API does not promise ('the exact class is unspecified and subject to change'). The candidate body set compatible with the site is every class implementing java.util.List; no fully-qualified path to a body is written, no locally written token forbids override, and no per-candidate equivalence record exists, so H3's exclusions do not reach it. This is the identical event Kotlin was charged for as a separate hidden item ('the body executed by the indexed read's get is chosen from the run-time class of the list, which that site does not name') and Python was charged for (`items[0]` dispatches to type(items).__getitem__). C++ and Swift correctly charge nothing because vector::operator[] and Array's subscript are statically resolved; Java is in Kotlin's and Python's position, not C++'s. The existing H6 nullability charge and the recorded refusal of H7 are unaffected and stand.
